thread:
Maria K: heads-up — Customer FinSuite reporting p95/p99 generation latency regressions since ~09:00 UTC. They see big tail spikes (p99 ~2.8s, baseline ~350ms). Raised via support ticket INC-2026-432. attaching screenshots and traces: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/fin-prod-latency?orgId=1

Ajay S: thx. can you paste an example request id and model/route? any config changes around 09:00?

Maria K: Request ids: rq_8f3a2c, rq_8f3a6f. Route: /v1/generate model: open-llama-13b-v2 quantized. No customer-side changes reported. We did an infra tweak in the continuous-batching service at 08:55 — reduced max_wait_ms from 20 -> 6 to improve median latency for high-qps customers (PR #4823).

Carmen D: ah. that was the rollout I did. The idea was to reduce median for big tenants but i flagged it in the patch notes that small tenants could regress. didnt expect this severity.

Leo T: quick note — reducing max_wait_ms can increase unfilled batch flush frequency which hurts throughput and increases tail when requests arrive in bursts or when KV cache cold-starts. we've seen this before.

Ajay S: can we confirm batch size distribution and flush rates around the incident? PromQL I ran: 
```
sum(rate(continuous_batcher_flush_total[5m])) by (pool)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(continuous_batcher_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
```
Grafana shows flush rate for low-qps pools doubled after 08:55, avg batch size dropped from 10 -> 2.

sre-bot: Incident created INC-2026-432 | severity=P2 | assignees=@ajay,@carmen | channel=#eng-sre

Carmen D: repro steps i used locally: spin up a single-worker small-qps workload and send poisson-ish traffic. script: 
```
# quick repro python
import time, requests, random
url = 'https://api.redwood.local/v1/generate'
for i in range(1000):
    payload = {'input':'hello'*random.randint(1,10)}
    requests.post(url, json=payload, headers={'X-Request-ID':f'repro-{i}'})
    time.sleep(random.expovariate(1/0.15))  # ~0.15s mean inter-arrival
```
That reproduces p99 ~2s with max_wait_ms=6, but p99 ~400ms with max_wait_ms=20.

Ajay S: nice. actionable check list: 1) rollback the 08:55 change 2) enable per-route hold-window for FinSuite while we investigate 3) run a canary load to verify p99 recovers 4) follow up with permanent config (adaptive_wait or qps-based policy).

Maria K: Support Ops, do we have a customer-facing blurb ready? They want ETA.

Support Ops: Draft: "We're investigating increased generation latency affecting a subset of customers. We've identified a recent batching configuration change and are applying mitigations. We'll update within 30 minutes and share a timeline for a permanent fix." happy to send once ajay confirms mitigation. :thumbsup:

Ajay S: i'm applying the rollback to continuous-batcher config now (rolling restart of pool small-qps-1). command: 
```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.redwood.local/configs/continuous-batcher/rollback \ 
  -d '{"change_id":"pr4823","env":"prod"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}'
```
Monitoring watch: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abcd/fin-prod-latency?from=now-1h&to=now

Leo T: while rolling, add a temporary rule to route FinSuite to a dedicated pool with higher max_wait (30ms) so they don't hit small batches. you can set per-customer override via: 
```
redwoodctl routes update --customer finsuite --batch.max_wait_ms 30
```

Ajay S: rollback completed on small-qps pools — restarted 6 workers. Watching flush rate and p99.

(10m later) Ajay S: early numbers: p99 for FinSuite dropped from 2.8s -> 420ms, p95 back to ~320ms. flush rate normalized, avg batch size increased back to ~9.

Carmen D: pushed a follow-up change to add adaptive_wait that scales max_wait_ms by instantaneous qps (PR #4889). will run canary in staging tomorrow.

Support Ops: Sent interim update to customer and attached note about rollback + workaround. Customer acknowledged and said they'll monitor.

Maria K: good job team. next steps: 1) keep watch for 2h 2) add regression alert for average batch size decreasing below threshold (per-route) 3) schedule postmortem if similar spike reappears.

Leo T: i'll add a Prometheus rule: 
```
- alert: BatcherAvgSizeLow
  expr: avg_over_time(continuous_batcher_avg_batch_size[5m]) < 3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "Batcher avg size low for >5m"
```

Ajay S: also adding a canary test in our nightly job that runs the poisson-ish load against a staging pool when we change batching params.

Maria K: closing this thread for now — last update at 1718006142. reopen if anything pops.
